2022_271_8_a_barton_malow_proposal_propo.paragraph: Barton Malow Builders submitted a proposal for construction management services on the Troy School District 2022 Bond Program, organized in five sections covering project approach, firm experience, team resumes, staffing plan, and BIM/VDC services. The firm cites more than 30 years of work in Troy across 12 elementary, 4 middle and 4 high schools plus the Early Childhood Center completed in 2019. The staffing plan prices a 146-month construction phase against a $555,000,000 program with $431,935,093 in trades plus general conditions, yielding total management costs of $29,672,393, estimated field general conditions of $14,335,996, and a total CM and GC cost of $44,008,389 against a total CM/GC budget of $44,011,507.
2022_271_8_a_barton_malow_proposal_propo.page:
OVERVIEW
Proposal for Construction Services, Troy School District 2022 Bond Program, submitted by Barton Malow Builders. The cover page is dated July 8, 2021; page footers and the staffing plan carry the date July 8, 2022. Contents are organized as Section 1 Project Approach Narrative, Section 2 Relevant Firm Experience, Section 3 Project Organizational Chart and Team Resumes, Section 4 Staffing Plan, and Section 5 Utilizing BIM and VDC.

APPROACH
Barton Malow states its team spent over 30 successful years working in the Troy School District, implementing improvements at 12 elementary, 4 middle and 4 high schools plus a new preschool building, the Early Childhood Center, completed in 2019. The narrative covers design phase leadership, constructability review, cost estimation across Schematic Design, Design Development and Construction Documents, a Cost Control Log, value engineering, minimizing interruptions in occupied buildings, MIOSHA-compliant safety oversight by a Safety Manager, bid packaging, e-bidding with livestream bid openings and cloud-based plan rooms, procurement using the Pype submittal register, four-stage change management tracked in SAP (PCO, COR, PCCO, SCCO), punchlist and closeout with final close-out typically required within 30 days of punchlist completion, weekly close-out meetings starting at the 90% completion mark, digital turnover via AutoDesk Build, and all change orders issued, approved and billed no later than 90 days after substantial completion.

WORKFORCE AND BIDDING METRICS
The Barton Malow Boot Camp, created in 2016, is a 6-week paid, 120-hour work experience program for area residents ages 18 to 24, with each participant assigned a mentor who spends 2 days per week on site. Bidder participation over the last 12 months is reported as 32 school districts, 157 unique projects, 68,856 solicitations to bids, 21,732 views, 4,089 bids received, and 5.20 bids per category.

BIM AND VDC
Section 5 describes BIM Execution Plan authoring, 3D constructability reviews using Autodesk Navisworks and BIM Track, model-based quantity takeoff, 3D clash detection, 4D scheduling linked to the live P6 schedule, site logistics planning, reality capture by laser scanning, drones and 360-degree cameras, virtual mock-ups, and as-built BIM handoff to IWMS/CMMS systems. Barton Malow states contingencies can be lowered a full 2% when BIM is implemented, and that BIM and the listed VDC services are additional services that can be discussed prior to contract award.
2022_271_8_a_barton_malow_proposal_propo.verbose:
Barton Malow Builders' Proposal for Construction Services addresses the Troy School District 2022 Bond Program. The cover page carries the date July 8, 2021, while every page footer and the staffing plan are dated July 8, 2022 (the staffing plan header reads Date: 7/8/22). The table of contents lists Section 1 Project Approach Narrative, Section 2 Relevant Firm Experience, Section 3 Project Organizational Chart and Team Resumes, Section 4 Staffing Plan, and Section 5 Utilizing BIM and VDC.

SECTION 1: PROJECT APPROACH NARRATIVE
Barton Malow opens by citing extensive knowledge of school construction and the fact that its team spent over 30 successful years working in the Troy School District, implementing improvements at all district facilities including 12 elementary, 4 middle and 4 high schools, plus a new preschool building, the Early Childhood Center, completed in 2019. The firm commits to involvement in all phases from pre-construction and design through close out, walking each project during design to identify existing conditions and minimize change orders and schedule delays, and meeting with the district's administrative team and building staff before work begins to discuss schedule and phasing.

Design phase: Barton Malow says it takes a leadership role rather than merely assisting, using in-house estimators, architects and engineers to manage the design process. It will establish a design phase schedule tied to bid dates, conduct design team meetings with published minutes, develop a set of Design Standards distributed to all Design Professionals, and perform constructability reviews. The design process is described in three major areas: Schematic Design, Design Development and Construction Documents. The Schematic Design Estimate provides more detail than the original Bond Application and is updated through Design Development, after which Barton Malow develops a very detailed estimate and creates a Cost Control Log documenting value engineering opportunities and possible bid alternates; the log continues to be updated during the Construction Document Phase. Barton Malow's Education group works exclusively with K-12 school districts.

Cost control and value engineering: value engineering is described as a team process evaluating all expenditures relating to construction, maintenance, operation and replacement, balancing performance and quality against initial and life-cycle costs, supported by in-house historical cost data and knowledge of the local market. The firm contrasts its continuous "design to a cost" methodology with traditional end-of-phase estimating.

Minimizing interruptions and safety: the narrative addresses renovating occupied facilities, developing a tentative work plan for administration approval and communicating it to staff, community and contractors, with zero tolerance for anyone failing to work within the plan. A Safety Manager conducts routine in-depth inspections, ensures compliance with Barton Malow safety policies and MIOSHA standards, and participates in MIOSHA inspections. Safety principles listed include zero tolerance for unsafe acts, a best-in-class safety culture with education, mentoring, empowerment and accountability, authority to STOP the job on any worker safety concern, working with subcontractors that share the firm's safety pursuit, and managing every incident to reduce impact on performance.

Bid packaging and technology: bid packages are developed early with the project divided into area and functional phases, tailored to involve local businesses, with long-lead-time items bid first and pre-purchase packages suggested where applicable. Prospective bidders go through a stringent prequalification process. Barton Malow describes itself as the first to market to harness e-bidding technology, livestream bid openings and cloud-based plan rooms, noting it solicited bids nearly every day of the State of Michigan "Stay Home/Stay Safe" executive order. The e-bidding workflow steps listed are bid advertisement, invitation to bid, prequalification, notification and distribution, document distribution, creation of the bid form, addenda, submission of bid security, submission of the bid, bid tabulation and audit trail. Bidder participation over the last 12 months is reported as 32 school districts, 157 unique projects, 68,856 solicitations to bids, 21,732 views, 4,089 bids received, and 5.20 bids per category.

Workforce development: the Barton Malow Boot Camp, created in 2016, is a 6-week paid work experience program for area residents between the ages of 18 and 24. The 120-hour program covers construction industry history and culture, financial literacy, OSHA and soft skills training, apprentice career paths, and on-the-job training in concrete and heavy civil work. Each boot camper is assigned a Barton Malow mentor, a skilled tradesperson on the project site, who spends 2 days per week with participants. Recruiting sources include the Barton Malow workforce database, career fairs, career and technical centers, vocational schools, technical colleges, building trade unions, employment service providers and labor management groups.

Procurement and change management: using the software system Pype, teams create a submittal register as soon as construction documents are issued, issue it with the bid documents, request long lead time information at post bid, and maintain a long lead register reviewed at each job progress meeting. Change management uses a disciplined four-stage approach; change status is tracked as Pending, Approved, or Approximate, and change issues move through four mechanisms: Potential Change Order (PCO), Change Order Request (COR), Prime Contract Change Order (PCCO) and Subcontractor Change Order (SCCO), all entered and tracked in the SAP cost management system, which tracks dollars, quantities, man-hours and schedule. Barton Malow states it places no mark-up on change orders and does not rely on outside agencies to validate change requests. Contractors that fail to comply may receive written notification, notice of contractual default and/or withholding of payment, with a jointly drafted corrective action plan. All final change orders are to be approved, written and billed by subcontractors within 90 days of substantial completion.

Punchlist, closeout and activation: pre-punchlists with required correction dates are generated before the design team's official punchlist. Close-out timelines are set for each bid package, with final close-out typically required within 30 days from completion of all punchlist items; weekly close-out meetings begin at the 90% completion mark. Digital turnover of closeout documents is provided through AutoDesk Build. The Activation Phase covers start-up and testing of systems, training of building engineers and maintenance staff, final completion and occupancy, turnover of keys, manuals, record drawings and maintenance stocks, and securing guarantees, affidavits, releases, bonds and waivers. Final billings include all change orders issued, approved and included no later than 90 days after substantial completion.

SECTION 2: RELEVANT FIRM EXPERIENCE
Bloomfield Hills School District, New High School, Bloomfield Hills, MI: $65,000,000, completion December 2015, project size 372,000 SF. The community approved a bond in May 2012 to renovate Andover High School, consolidating Lahser and Andover into Bloomfield Hills High School, with a 220,000 SF addition including learning communities, commons space, full service kitchen, full production performing arts center, swimming pool and competition gymnasium (about 150,000 SF). Contact: Christina Kostiuk, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, 248/341-5452.

Romeo Community Schools, 2016 Bond Program, Romeo, MI: $86,000,000, scheduled June 2021. Scope includes renovations to the Romeo Engineering and Technology Center (RETC) at Romeo High School, conversion of Powell Middle School into a 9th grade facility, conversion of Romeo High School into the new Romeo Middle School with a 6-8 configuration, upgrades at multiple elementary schools, Barnabo Athletic Field stadium and field upgrades with new concessions, team room, toilet facilities and bus loop, and relocation of the running track at Memorial Field. Contact: Todd Robinson, Superintendent, 586/752-0200.

Midland Public Schools, Midland, MI: $120,400,000, scheduled completion April 2021. In 2015, with Barton Malow Company and French Associates, Inc., Midland Public Schools passed a 3.95 mill increase bond issue. Since the first series of bonds were sold in July of 2015, Barton Malow has put in place $44M in construction, opened a new elementary school and two completely renovated elementary schools with 10,000 SF additions. Contact: Michael Sharrow, 989/923-5014.

Romulus Community Schools, Sinking Fund, Romulus, MI: $15,000,000, completion December 2028, covering elementary security, middle and high school technology, athletic field improvements, classroom audio and visual systems at the high school, roofs, boilers, parking lots, lighting and student common spaces. Contact: Bill Garland, Operations Manager, 734/532-1602.

Utica Community Schools, 2009 Bond Program, Sterling Heights, MI: $50,000,000, completion February 2014, project size 51,000 SF (high school). Work included renovation of Utica High School, a new administrative building, new gym and athletic office, hallway and locker renovations, smart-boards, a new media center, main office relocation, new science labs, corridor upgrades, a new facade along Shelby Road, and major mechanical and electrical upgrades. Contact: Bob Monroe, Superintendent, 586/797-1000.

GISD Career Center, Flint, MI: $13,000,000, completion December 2016. With designers Stantec, Phase I featured over 77,000 square feet of renovations supporting STEM work with 3D printers and fume hoods; Phase II delivered the Innovation Zone, an 8,700-square-foot addition connecting the south and north wings. Contact: Dr. Keely Mounger, Deputy Superintendent.

Chippewa Valley Schools, Bond Program, Clinton Township, MI: $89,765,000, completion December 2014, project size 2,671,711. Barton Malow has partnered with the district since 1979; the 2010 Bond Program is the fourth consecutive program after 1997, 2001 and 2004, providing all 24 district facilities with improvements including security cameras, surveillance systems, expanded card access, bus replacements, roof replacements, parking lot work and equipment and furniture replacement. Barton Malow is also working with the district on a $50,000,000 Bond Program scheduled for completion in 2023. Contact: Scott Sederlund, Superintendent, 586/723-2000.

Waterford School District, Bond Program, Waterford, MI: $100,000,000, completion 2021. Residents approved a $100 million bond program in 2016. Every elementary school was renovated, with parking lot reconfigurations and new gymnasium additions; athletic field upgrades occurred at Kettering and Mott High Schools including new turf baseball and softball fields with new dugouts, plus transportation facility improvements and secured access and security camera upgrades. Contact: Scott Lindberg, Superintendent, 248/682-7800.

Roseville Community Schools, 2018 Bond Program, Roseville, MI: $60,000,000, completion December 2021, focused on instructional technology and infrastructure, school security and student safety, and upgrades to athletic fields, playgrounds and parking lots. Contact: Mark Blaszkowski, Superintendent, 586/879-3133.

Marygrove, Early Education Center, Detroit, MI: $16,000,000, completion May 2021. In November 2019 Marygrove Conservancy and partners broke ground on a P-20 initiative on a historic 53-acre landscape in Northwest Detroit. The one-story, 28,000 square-foot childcare center, built on an existing parking lot, features 12 classrooms, observation rooms, a library and a health therapy room, and is operated by Starfish Family Services. Contact: Rachel Sikora, Owner's Representative, 410/404-6196.

SECTION 3: ORGANIZATIONAL CHART AND TEAM RESUMES
Barton Malow states it has specialized in education construction projects since 1925. The executive team and project structure list Mike Stobak, Vice President; Larry Bukowski, Project Executive; Juan Vazquez, General Superintendent (construction); Lauren Bukowski, Senior Project Manager; Josh Eisenman, Project Manager; and Araceli Pompa, Senior Cost Analyst, organized under Project Leadership, Operations Team 1, Operations Team 2 and Project Support.

Mike Stobak, Vice President of Barton Malow's Education Group, has 34 years of experience, holds a Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering from Lawrence Technological University, is Safe2Work Certified and OSHA 30-Hour Certified, and has been a Board Member of Romeo Community Schools since being elected in 2007. His relevant experience includes Troy School District 2019 Sinking Fund, Romeo Community Schools 2016 Bond Program, Livonia Public Schools, Roseville Community Schools 2018 Bond Program, Bloomfield Hills School District sinking fund projects and the new Bloomfield Hills High School, Waverly Community Schools (Lansing), Anchor Bay School District 2017 Bond Program, Spring Lake Public Schools 2014 Bond Program, Beecher Community School District (Flint) 2013 Bond Program, Ann Arbor Public Schools 2012 Technology Bond Series 1, Midland Public Schools and Romulus Community Schools.

Larry Bukowski, LEED AP, Project Executive, describes himself as a resident of Troy and a parent of three daughters. His profile states 22 years of experience in the construction industry covering project management, estimating and preparing plans and specifications; the resume sidebar lists 18 years of experience. He holds an MBA, a Graduate Certificate in Project Management, and a Bachelor of Science in Construction Management, all from Lawrence Technological University, and LEED AP BD+C from the U.S. Green Building Council. Relevant experience includes Troy School District 2019 Sinking Fund, South Redford School District 2016 Sinking Fund, Huron Valley Schools 2019 Bond Issue, Royal Oak Community Schools 2015 Sinking Fund Projects, Southfield Public Schools 2020 Sinking Fund Projects, Waterford School District 2016 and 2020 Bond Programs, and School District of the City of Pontiac 2020 Bond Program.

Juan Vazquez III, General Superintendent, has 26 years of experience with expertise in renovations and client-occupied sites. He is pursuing a Bachelor of Science degree in Construction Management at Lawrence Technological University in Southfield, Michigan, completed a four-year carpenter apprenticeship program to Journeyman status, holds Certified Industrial Technician status, CAMTEC Construction Industry Tech, CAMTEC Basic Estimating I, CAMTEC OSHA-MIOSHA 10 hr Construction Safety Course and CAMTEC Blueprint Reading I, and is OSHA 30-Hour Certified and Safe2Work Certified. Relevant experience includes Waterford School District bond projects, Bloomfield Hills School District sinking fund projects and new high school, Utica Community Schools capital improvement program and 2009 Bond Program, Heritage Junior High School and 2003 bond projects.

Lauren Bukowski, PE, Senior Project Manager, is a current resident of Troy and a graduate of Troy High School; her sidebar lists 17 years of experience. She holds a Master of Business Administration (2012), a Graduate Certificate in Project Management (2012) and a Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering (2009), all from Lawrence Technological University, and is a Registered Professional Engineer in Michigan, with training in Lead and Asbestos Awareness, Masonry Wall Bracing, Planning and Scheduling, Safe Start, OSHA 30-Hour Certification and OSHA Crane Standard Revisions. Relevant experience includes Bloomfield Hills Schools (Bowers Farm Schoolhouse, new high school, 2017 Sinking Fund), Troy School District 2004 Bond and Technology Program, Huron Valley Schools 2019 Bond Issue, South Redford School District 2016 Sinking Fund, Oakland Community College, Southfield Public Schools, Troy Beaumont Hospital North Bed Tower Addition, the Dequindre Bridge, and Royal Oak Community Schools board office relocation and remodeling.

Josh Eisenman, Project Manager, holds a Bachelors Degree in Environmental Engineering from Michigan State University; his sidebar lists 2 years of experience. Relevant experience includes Roseville Community Schools 2018 Bond Program, Spring Lake Public Schools 2014 Bond Program, Marygrove Conservancy Liberal Arts Renovation, and Flat Rock Community Schools 2022 ESSER Funds Projects.

Araceli Pompa, Senior Cost Analyst, administers accounting functions at the project site and reports to upper management and project controllers. Her profile states over 15 years of experience; her sidebar lists 17 years. She holds an Accounting Certificate from Massachusetts Bay Community College and is pursuing an Associates degree in Accounting. Relevant experience includes Waterford School District bond projects, Bloomfield Hills School District new high school, Armada School District, Southfield School District and Imlay City School District bond programs.

SECTION 5: UTILIZING BIM + VDC
Barton Malow describes a holistic, value-driven approach to Virtual Design and Construction organized around Discover (data collection and registration), Develop (content and creation, workflow), Analyze (collaborative analysis and continuous refinement) and Share (information distribution and monitoring). Services include BIM Execution Plan authoring, 3D model development, 3D constructability reviews analyzing spatial configurations, clearances, accessibility, floor-to-floor heights, building system configurations and long lead-time items such as steel using Autodesk Navisworks and BIM Track, model-based quantity takeoff and scope visualization, 3D clash detection, 4D model-based scheduling with model objects linked to activities in the live P6 construction schedule, site logistics planning, reality capture using laser scanning, drones and 360-degree panoramic cameras, virtual mock-ups and walkthroughs, and as-built BIM with data integration into the Owner's IWMS/CMMS solutions. Under cost savings, Barton Malow states that contingencies can be lowered a full 2% when BIM is implemented, and that BIM and the other VDC services listed are additional services that can be discussed prior to contract award.

2022_272_8_a_fielding_international_prop.paragraph: Fielding International, an education design and architecture firm at 460 Hilton Road, Ferndale, Michigan 48220, proposed Education Design Services to Troy School District to re-imagine middle school teaching and learning. The July 15, 2022 letter is addressed to Assistant Superintendent Christine DiPalato at 440 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, and outlines three phases running from August through December, with optional follow-on implementation work in 2023. Total cost for Learning Design Services is $89,100, with reimbursable travel expenses not to exceed $20,000.
2022_272_8_a_fielding_international_prop.page:
PARTIES AND DATE
Fielding International (460 Hilton Road, Ferndale, Michigan 48220; fieldingintl.com; offices listed as Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Rhode Island and Singapore) submitted an Education Design Services proposal dated July 15, 2022 to Ms. Christine DiPalato, Assistant Superintendent, Troy School District, 440 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Interior pages are headed "Troy School District Proposal June 20, 2022." The proposal is signed by Michael Posthumus, Education Design Principal (mike.posthumus@fieldingintl.com), and includes a signature block for acceptance.

SCOPE
The engagement supports Troy School District as it explores a new vision for middle school teaching and learning, auditing staff and student perceptions, designing a new learning ecosystem concept including physical space concepts, and transitioning into a process-consulting phase alongside District leadership.

PHASE 1: PRE-DISCOVERY AND FRAMING
Gathers contextual information on current middle school programs. Includes a kick-off meeting, asynchronous data collection and surveys, visioning and prioritization workshops, and one-on-one 30-minute virtual meetings with school leaders. Ideal interview candidates are the building leaders at the four middle schools in Troy plus District leaders. Proposed activities are scheduled for August.

PHASE 2: PROGRAM AND ENVIRONMENT DISCOVERY
Centered on a multi-day immersive site visit (a 3-4 day onsite visit) with structured observations and informal interviews with students, teachers and staff, plus presentation of exemplar school models and an optional, highly recommended visit by Troy staff to another innovative school. Deliverable: Teaching, Learning, and Future Facilities Discovery Report, presented virtually to a selected "School Design Team." Activities September through October; report development September-October; virtual report delivery October.

PHASE 3: RE-IMAGINING SCHOOL, A DEEP DIVE
Builds common understanding and then re-designs the school experience. Comprises 2 Building Common Understanding workshop days, 3 Design Workshop days, and 7 remote planning and reporting sessions across five sessions covering Students of the 21st Century, youth aspirations, the science of adolescent learning, teaching and learning in the 21st century, school mission and culture, alignment of mission/culture/programs/physical space, student and staff agency, partnerships and networks, and re-imagining time, space and technology. Deliverable: Learning Ecosystem Concept Design. Activities October through December; refinement November-December; report delivered December.

FUTURE OPPORTUNITIES (NOT INCLUDED)
Preparing for Implementation and Change Leadership using "Process Consulting" as defined by the Society for Process Consulting, proposed for January 2023 through June 2023 and beyond: Winter 2023 with 3-4 workshop days plus remote support; Spring 2023 with 2-3 workshop days; Summer 2023 with 1-2 workshop days, ending with a Teaching, Learning, and Leading for the Future Guidebook. Architectural Design services are also offered; Fielding notes it is currently teamed with local architects for Ann Arbor Public Schools and Portage Public Schools in Michigan. One paragraph references "the opportunity in front of Holly Area Schools."

FEES

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Phase 1: Pre-Discovery | (no fee stated) |
| Phase 2: Discovery | $34,500 |
| Phase 3: Re-Imagining Middle School | $54,600 |
| Total cost for Learning Design Services | $89,100 |
| Reimbursable travel expenses | Not-to-exceed $20,000 |

TERMS
Invoices sent monthly for a percentage of work completed by phase, payment due within 15 days. All travel expenses reimbursed at cost without markup; printing and workshop materials reimbursed at cost without markup. Travel covers airfare, lodging and meals for up to three to four Learning Designers, some traveling from out of state.
2022_272_8_a_fielding_international_prop.verbose:
Fielding International submitted a proposal for Education Design Services to the Troy School District. The cover letter is dated July 15, 2022 and addressed to Ms. Christine DiPalato, Assistant Superintendent, Troy School District, 440 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Fielding's letterhead reads "Designing schools where learners Thrive," 460 Hilton Road, Ferndale, Michigan 48220 USA, fieldingintl.com, with locations listed as Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Rhode Island and Singapore. Interior pages carry the running head "Troy School District Proposal June 20, 2022." The proposal closes with a signature from Michael Posthumus, Education Design Principal (mike.posthumus@fieldingintl.com), and an acceptance block for signature, name/title and date. Fielding states that upon signed acceptance it can begin work immediately.

PURPOSE
The engagement supports Troy School District as it explores a new vision for what middle school teaching and learning might look like now and in the future. Based on previous conversations, Fielding outlines a scope facilitating engagement and planning to form a vision representing a shift in teaching and learning practice priorities better aligned with the District's objectives for strong interdisciplinary programming that also supports student wellness and social-emotional learning. The work begins with auditing staff and student perceptions of the school experience, uses those insights to explore and design ways to transform the school experience with a new learning ecosystem concept including physical space concepts, and finally transitions into a process-consulting phase in which Fielding's educators and designers work alongside District leadership and key staff for detailed planning, implementation and sustaining success. The letter frames the opportunity as creating a flexible and innovative school program and learning environments centered on what is meaningful and relevant to young people, arguing that the existing model of education no longer meets the diverse needs of students.

PHASE 1: PRE-DISCOVERY AND FRAMING
This phase gathers contextual information to understand the current state of Troy School District middle school programs and aspirations for a re-imagined future. It begins with meetings and data collection. The Fielding Team will host one-on-one 30-minute virtual meetings with a selection of school leaders to hear individual aspirations. Ideal interview candidates are the building leaders at the four middle schools in Troy, along with District leaders engaged in the rest of the process. Listed components are a Pre-Discovery kick-off meeting, asynchronous data collection and information gathering, visioning and prioritization workshops, and virtual meetings with focused 1:1 interviews with District leaders. The stated objective is to collect data and observations to complete a Teaching and Learning Audit Discovery Report serving as the foundation for future work. Site visits and proposed activities are scheduled for August and include virtual kick-off and progress/status meetings, data collection through surveys and asynchronous resource gathering, and focus group and individual interviews.

PHASE 2: PROGRAM AND ENVIRONMENT DISCOVERY
The main component is a multi-day immersive site visit by Fielding International team members, during which the team completes structured observations of the middle school experience and conducts informal interviews with students, teachers and staff to capture quantitative and qualitative data on how teaching and learning experiences are delivered, and to identify misalignments between the aspirations of District and school leaders, physical learning environments, and the actual student experience. The team debriefs immediate findings with the District at the end of the visit. Fielding will also introduce school models demonstrating future-ready physical school designs and programmatic approaches to middle years learning; a school site visit from Troy to another school implementing innovative approaches is described as optional and highly recommended.

The Phase Two deliverable is the Teaching, Learning, and Future Facilities Discovery Report, synthesizing information gathered during Program and Environment Discovery, highlighting the core pillars of the future of Troy School District, misalignments between current practice and future aspirations, and priority areas of growth. The report relies on first-hand data including interviews and observations from the site visits and documents middle school learning models existing in other schools or programs. A virtual Discovery Report presentation to a selected "School Design Team" and other desired stakeholders takes place once the report is complete, ending phase two.

Phase 2 components are listed as Discovery kick-off, visioning, multi-day on-site Discovery Visit, and Discovery Report Presentation. Site visits and proposed activities are scheduled for September through October and include leadership kickoff, a visioning workshop, student/staff/leadership focus groups and interviews, middle school program and facility observations, school model exemplar presentations and workshops, and Fielding team data synthesis. Report development is September-October with virtual report delivery in October.

PHASE 3: RE-IMAGINING SCHOOL, A DEEP DIVE
Following Discovery, Fielding facilitates a process helping students, staff and community members re-imagine the learning experience in Troy School District middle school programs. Two components are building a shared understanding of the problems and opportunities facing the District and its students, followed by conceptually re-designing the school experience. The Teaching, Learning, and Future Facilities Discovery Report serves as the foundational document.

Common Understanding consists of workshops leading the School Design Team and potentially an expanded stakeholder group through learning experiences about Students in the 21st Century and post-COVID, reviewing research on the science of adolescent learning, the experiences and aspirations of today's youth, and place-based community needs, using models and case studies of innovative school programs. Design consists of constructive workshops to create a new vision for school, including identifying how mission and culture may need to change, exploring new teaching and learning strategies, empowering students and teachers with agency, using partnerships and networks, and restructuring time, space and technology. Both programs and physical learning environments are addressed.

The Phase Three deliverable is the Learning Ecosystem Concept Design, a narrative describing ideal conditions for learning in a re-imagined Troy School District school, with embedded images and precedent examples of schools already implementing components of the vision.

Phase 3 is structured as 2 Building Common Understanding workshop days, 3 Design Workshop days, and 7 remote planning and reporting sessions. Site visits and proposed activities run October through December. Session 1 covers "Who are the Students of the 21st Century?" (Learn/Reflect Workshop) and Youth Aspirations and Experiences (Design/Produce Workshop). Session 2 covers the Science of Adolescent Learning and Teaching and Learning in the 21st Century. Session 3 covers Establishing the Framework for a New School Mission and Culture and Exploring Alignment between Mission, Culture, Programs, and Physical Space. Session 4 covers Cultivating Student and Staff Agency and Creating the Conditions for Engagement, and Partnerships and Networks to Support a new Mission and Culture. Session 5 covers Re-imagining the Use of Time, Space and Technology and Final Reflections and Summary of the Work. Learning Ecosystem Concept refinement occurs November-December with the report delivered in December.
